title: Career Roadmap · Cloud Support Technician
summary: A Cloud Support Technician helps maintain cloud-based systems, troubleshoot access and connectivity issues, monitor services, and support virtual machines, storage, networks and user accounts.

facts.Course: Diploma - Cyber Security / AI / Data Analytics / Cloud

about.label: Common pathway
about.text: Class 10/12 → IT / Computer diploma or related degree → networking and cloud labs → IT Support / Cloud Support role → Cloud Administrator or Cloud Engineer.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: Science with Mathematics is useful; other streams may qualify for some IT diplomas and entry-level training.

blocks.label: Useful subjects
blocks.text: Computer Science, Mathematics, English and basic electronics.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Computer hardware, networking, Linux, virtualization and cloud computing.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Troubleshooting, logical reasoning, documentation and customer communication.

blocks.label: Entrance
blocks.text: Polytechnic and degree admissions depend on state and institution; verify current official notifications.

items.text: Diploma in Computer Engineering / IT → IT support, networking and infrastructure fundamentals.
Diploma in Cloud Computing / Networking → Cloud support and administration foundations; confirm course recognition and lab access.
BCA / B.Sc. Computer Science or IT → Systems support, cloud operations and technical support.
B.Tech. Computer Science / IT → Broader cloud engineering and infrastructure pathways.
B.Sc. Cybersecurity / Networking → Security-focused infrastructure support.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: Eligibility and entrance processes vary. A relevant diploma can be a starting point; degree requirements differ by employer and role.

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Computer hardware, operating systems, networking and command-line basics.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Linux, virtualization, cloud storage, identity/access management and troubleshooting.

blocks.label: Year 3
blocks.text: Cloud monitoring, backups, security fundamentals, automation and internship experience.

blocks.label: Year 4, if applicable
blocks.text: Cloud project portfolio, advanced certification preparation and job applications.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Deploy a basic cloud-hosted website; configure user permissions; set up cloud storage and backups; create a virtual network and monitoring alerts.

blocks.label: Government / education
blocks.text: College IT departments, research computing teams and eligible public-sector IT projects.

blocks.label: Private sector
blocks.text: Managed service providers, cloud service partners, IT support companies and corporate infrastructure teams.

blocks.label: Potential employers
blocks.text: AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud partners and IT service providers; check official careers pages.

blocks.label: Ideal areas
blocks.text: Cloud operations, infrastructure support, monitoring, networking and technical help desk.
Internships and placements are not guaranteed.

blocks.text: Useful certifications

blocks.label: Microsoft Certified
blocks.text:
Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) — foundational cloud concepts and Azure services.
Microsoft Learn
+1

items.text: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner — foundational AWS cloud knowledge; check the current exam guide.
Cisco CCST Networking — networking fundamentals.
CompTIA Network+ — vendor-neutral networking knowledge.

blocks.text: Start with one cloud platform and build hands-on labs before pursuing multiple certifications. Verify current exam details and fees with the provider.
